title: Distinct normalized projections off a unit vector
statement:
Let $u,v,w$ be unit vectors in a real inner product space satisfying $\langle v,uangle \le 0$, $\langle w,uangle \le 0$, and $\langle v,wangle \le 0$, and suppose that neither $v$ nor $w$ equals $u$ or $-u$ and that $v 
eq w$. For $x$ in the space write $\pi(x) = x - \langle u,xangle\,u$ for the projection of $x$ onto the orthogonal complement of $\mathrm{span}\{u\}$. Then the two normalized projections $
orm{\pi(v)}^{-1}\,\pi(v)$ and $
orm{\pi(w)}^{-1}\,\pi(w)$ cannot be equal.
hypotheses_covered: u, v, w are unit vectors
inner product of v and u is nonpositive
inner product of w and u is nonpositive
inner product of v and w is nonpositive
v is not equal to u
w is not equal to u
v is not equal to w
replaced:
Let $u,v,w$ be unit vectors with $\langle v,u\rangle \le 0$, $\langle w,u\rangle \le 0$,
$\langle v,w\rangle \le 0$, with $v,w \notin \{u,-u\}$ and $v \neq w$. Then the
normalized projections $\norm{\mathrm{orthProj}(u,v)}^{-1}\mathrm{orthProj}(u,v)$ and
$\norm{\mathrm{orthProj}(u,w)}^{-1}\mathrm{orthProj}(u,w)$ cannot be equal
(the statement derives a contradiction from their equality).
